clue.text: Preparing spinach or escalopes includes routine tasks

parts.note: surface padding: it makes the kitchen scene and supplies no letters

indicators.note: the phrase before it is said to contain the answer within its run of letters

parts.note: found across the end of spinach, the whole of or, and the start of escalopes

explanation.surface: A cook's everyday kitchen work: getting the spinach ready or the escalopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preparing' looks like an anagram signal, but it is only surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Chores are the regular household jobs that have to be done, a plain synonym for routine tasks.

clue.text: Old coin representing only part of monarch?

parts.note: half is only a portion of something
the Crown stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A coin that shows just a piece of a king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: A half crown was a British coin worth two shillings and sixpence, withdrawn in 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: The half crown was a pre-decimal British coin, so it is a historic piece of currency.

clue.text: Run back! Ebbing East River is on turn

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the next pair of letters runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
R is the map abbreviation for river
to wind is to turn, as with a key or a handle

explanation.surface: A cry to run backwards as the tide turns on a river in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewind a tape or film is to run it backwards to an earlier point.

clue.text: Team demonstrations are not the main event

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase is meant: things that are not the main event

parts.note: a side is a sports team
shows are displays or demonstrations

explanation.surface: A team's exhibition matches are only warm-up acts before the real fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideshows are minor attractions at a fair or circus, secondary diversions beside the principal spectacle.

clue.text: Pester an animal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to nag someone persistently
second meaning: a burrowing black-and-white mammal

explanation.surface: Someone is annoying a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to harass with repeated demands, and the noun names a nocturnal burrowing mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: This guitarist sounds fishy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Julian ..., the English classical guitarist

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun: a fish
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A musician whose name rings suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds fishy' means suspicious, but here it says the guitarist's name is also a fish; nothing is a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Bream was a celebrated classical guitarist, and a bream is a deep-bodied freshwater fish.

clue.text: Relied on quiet end indeed

parts.note: read as in + deed: the pieces before go in the word deed
P is piano, the musical marking for soft
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone counted on a peaceful conclusion, and it came.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be split into two words, in and deed, the first placing P and END inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to trust and count on them, so the past tense matches relied on.

clue.text: Vote for English and confused Celt

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a confused thing is jumbled, so the letters of the next word are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing between an English candidate and a bewildered Scot or Welshman at the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect someone is to choose them by ballot, which is what casting a vote for a candidate does.

clue.text: Gave permission for everyone with nothing to marry

parts.note: everyone means all of them
the letter O looks like zero
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Someone gave the go-ahead for anybody, even the penniless, to get married.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something is to permit it, so the past tense matches granting permission for something.

clue.text: It's symbolic how I get all involved in Lego car crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so all the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, except that the grid needs an O where Lego has its E

explanation.surface: Someone explains the deeper meaning of joining in a toy-brick car pile-up.
explanation.walkthrough: I, all and Lego car rearranged spell ALLEGORICAL, meaning symbolic; the grid's ALLOGORICAL, with O for E, is a setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegorical writing uses characters and events to stand for abstract ideas, so it is symbolic in nature.

clue.text: Train to put into words

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fast train making few stops
second meaning: to voice or state a thought

explanation.surface: An instruction to teach someone how to articulate things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a verb, to coach, but it is the noun: a fast service with few stops.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast service stopping at few stations, and to express an idea is to state it in language.

clue.text: Seasonal tidy-up is bound to upset Lance

parts.note: to spring is to leap or bound

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the name are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A yearly clear-out is sure to annoy a man called Lance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain', as in 'bound to', but it is the verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring clean is a thorough cleaning of a house traditionally done each year in the spring.

clue.text: Mythical creature smothers clones found scattered round pole

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the following item, enclosing it
things scattered are thrown about in disorder, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
N for north, one of the magnetic poles

explanation.surface: A legendary beast suffocates a group of duplicates spread out around a post.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of smothers and clones are rearranged and N goes in after LOCH to make LOCH NESS MONSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the legendary beast said to live in a Scottish lake, an example of a creature from myth.

clue.text: Go west round lake for warmth

indicators.note: the first words wrap around the next item, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
W is the compass abbreviation for west
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Advice to travel westward around a lake to find some heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is just GO followed by W, with L tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a gentle radiated heat or a warm feeling, so it can stand for warmth.

clue.text: Appearance of obsession I take on

indicators.note: the speaker takes on something, i.e. adds it after the preceding pieces

parts.note: a complex is a psychological fixation
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits to taking on the look of an obsessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Complexion means the natural look and colour of the skin of the face, hence general aspect or appearance.

clue.text: Actor hopes to win crown

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who pretends, plays a part

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: one who hopes to win the crown
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a claimant to a throne

explanation.surface: A performer dreams of becoming king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Pretender and Young Pretender were the Stuart claimants to the British throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is someone who fakes, as an actor does, and also a person claiming a throne they do not hold.

clue.text: I'm going quietly to the finish — something bad's about to happen

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
P is piano, the musical marking for soft
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone slips away silently to the end, sensing doom approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Impending describes an event, usually unwelcome, that is imminent and looming close.

clue.text: Understood demon to be legal

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Someone grasped that a devil was within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understood' reads as a verb but is the adjective, as in an understood agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied without being stated, that is, tacitly understood.

clue.text: Call boy who is in charge of circus performances

definitions.text: who is in charge of circus performances
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person, 'one who is in charge'

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
Master is the old courtesy title for a young boy

explanation.surface: Summon the lad who runs the big top show.
explanation.walkthrough: Master is the traditional formal title for a boy, as in 'Master John Smith' on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster is the person who introduces the acts and directs the show in the circus ring.

clue.text: Eurydice, Persephone, Icarus and Chloe initially appear in heroic poem

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each name is used

parts.note: the first letters of the four names

explanation.surface: Figures from Greek myth turn up in a grand narrative poem, as they often do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' between the names is just joining them; it supplies no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem celebrating the deeds of heroes, like the Iliad or Odyssey.

clue.text: Brother goes to arbitrators to solve noisy quarrel

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Brother or Father in religious orders
ACAS is Britain's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which settles industrial disputes

explanation.surface: A sibling takes a row to the mediators to have it settled.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the British public body that helps resolve disputes between employers and workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl, a loud row between people.

clue.text: Muddled brother lent coat to writer

indicators.note: muddled means mixed up, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A confused sibling handed his coat to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the novelist of Jane Eyre had a brother, Branwell, who was famously muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë was the English novelist who wrote Jane Eyre, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Accept outrage up to a point

parts.note: read as out + rage: out, meaning wrong, asks for the letters of rage to be reordered
E for east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Tolerating fury, but only so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrage' must be split into out and rage; 'up to a point' looks like 'partly' but means placed next to a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to something is to consent to it or go along with it, so it means accept.

clue.text: Claw involved in frontal onslaught

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: found across the end of frontal and the start of onslaught

explanation.surface: A claw plays its part in a head-on attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey, so it is a kind of claw.

clue.text: Heartless Lily meets Ric, a student. How poetic!

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is cut out, keeping only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name
taken as written
taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted girl meets a student called Ric, and someone sighs at the romance of it.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner's plate shown by a learner driver in Britain, so it stands for any student.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical describes expression that is song-like and full of feeling, a close synonym for poetic.

clue.text: Retract denial of it to police, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: to retract is to draw back, so the string that follows is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: no is a denial
the word it taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detective branch

explanation.surface: Someone takes back a statement they gave to the police, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase meaning 'so to speak', but 'manner of speaking' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's way of pronouncing and choosing words, that is, their style of speech.

clue.text: Poet almost takes on Buster

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
the shortened word takes something on, adding it at its end

parts.note: John Keats, the English Romantic poet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet very nearly takes on a tough guy called Buster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buster' looks like a slangy form of address but is the first name of a famous comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was the American silent-film comedian known for his deadpan face and stunts.

clue.text: Enlist again only to quit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sign on once more
second meaning: to give up a job or post

explanation.surface: A soldier rejoins the army and then promptly leaves it.
explanation.walkthrough: With a hyphen, re-sign means to sign up again; without one it means to step down.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to formally leave a position, and re-signing a contract is enlisting once more.
